pass_summary: This pass found only thin, mixed-quality Metabolic evidence for LGG. The one usable finding - stabilized HbA1c versus a placebo rise, in non-diabetic older adults - does not extend to existing type 2 diabetes, where a separate small trial found no fasting-glucose benefit. Lipid findings that surfaced were not gradeable for LGG specifically: one used a corn-fiber synbiotic that confounds attribution to the strain, and another used an unidentified L. rhamnosus product from a different manufacturer with no strain designation given, so it cannot be confirmed as GG. No strain-confirmed evidence was found for body weight, blood pressure, visceral fat, or NAFLD; the one gestational-diabetes trial in this literature used HN001, a different L. rhamnosus strain, not GG.

claims.population_detail: middle-aged/older adults without type 2 diabetes (HbA1c trajectory, not treatment of existing diabetes)
claims.effect_size: HbA1c stable on LGG vs increased on placebo over 90 days, F(1,90)=8.44, p=0.005
claims.tier_rationale: Single double-blind RCT (n=93 after exclusions from 200 enrolled), 90 days, no SR available. Scoped per tier rule 5 to the non-diabetic population it actually studied - a separate, smaller RCT in women with existing type 2 diabetes (n=34, 8 weeks, same 10x10^9 CFU/day dose) found no between-group difference in fasting glucose, so this finding should not be read as evidence LGG treats diagnosed diabetes. A single unreplicated RCT without formal bias appraisal caps this at B.
claims.notes: A separate RCT in women with existing type 2 diabetes (DOI:10.1007/s00394-023-03139-3, n=34) found no fasting-glucose benefit at the same dose. Not built as a second row - same impact_id/population pair - see tier_rationale.

gaps: met-ldl / met-total-cholesterol / met-triglycerides: a synbiotic trial (LGG + soluble corn fiber, Costabile et al. 2017, Saimes study) found reduced LDL and total cholesterol in hypercholesterolemic elderly, but the corn fiber co-intervention is itself cholesterol-lowering and the effect cannot be attributed to LGG alone under tier rule 2's logic; not built as a claim. A second trial (PMC11083618, n=50 Thai elderly, LDL -35.32 mg/dL p=0.045) used an L. rhamnosus product from a Korean manufacturer with no ATCC 53103/GG designation given - strain identity unconfirmed, so also not built as a claim, per the taxonomy trap noted in triage. met-body-weight: an LGG-specific RCT was not found; several body-weight trials surfaced are other Lactobacillus species. met-insulin-resistance: one finding (HOMA-IR improved in pregnancy) used an LGG+BB12 combination product, not decomposable to LGG alone per tier rule 2. met-gestational-diabetes: the well-known positive trial in this space is HN001, a distinct L. rhamnosus strain - not GG, not used here.
